quote: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
rationale: Section 20 meets the preferred position. Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer and its Affiliates for third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims relating to the Services or Deliverables (20.1) and for Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, bodily injury/property damage, unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud (20.2). Standard procedure (prompt notice, cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense, control of defence, prejudice-limited notice failure, settlement consent) appears in 20.4, and 20.5 adds the procure/modify/replace/refund remedy at Vendor's expense in addition to defence. Customer's reciprocal indemnity in 20.3 is appropriately narrow (unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorized, and Customer's violation of Applicable Law), with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modifications and combinations. Indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims under 21.3, so the Vendor indemnity is not squeezed by the liability cap — better than the fallback super-cap. No redline required.

verification.notes: No proposal: element-level redline verification is not applicable.

quote: 14.2 Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel.
rationale: The IP package sits at the preferred position. Section 14.2 gives us ownership of Deliverables with an express Vendor assignment (plus personnel assignments and further-assurance cooperation); Section 14.1 confirms we retain all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information and independently developed IP, with no transfer to Vendor beyond a limited processing right to deliver the Services; Section 14.3 lets Vendor retain only Vendor Technology and routes embedded Vendor Technology through the Section 13.2 perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, modify, create derivative works and permit contractors to support it; and Section 14.4 bars joint ownership absent a signed instrument and keeps feedback voluntary and non-identifying. Section 15.1 reinforces our data position by prohibiting sale, advertising use, cross-customer combination and model training without our written consent. No assignment of our IP or data to Vendor, no Vendor-owned deliverables without a licence back, and no joint ownership. Minor point noted only: the Section 14.1 processing right includes "improve the Services", though it is confined to providing the Services for us and is further limited by Section 15.1 — not a deviation.
ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data

verification.notes: No proposal: element-level redline verification is not applicable.

quote: 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates.
rationale: Section 24 meets our preferred position in full. Clause 24.1 gives us a consent-free right to assign to an Affiliate or to a successor by merger, reorganization, acquisition or substantially-all-assets sale (notice only). Clause 24.2 restricts Vendor assignment, delegation of material performance, and transfer by change of control to Customer's prior written consent (not unreasonably withheld) and bars assignment to a direct Customer competitor. Clause 24.3 applies a reasonable consent standard to other assignments, and clause 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees or reduce service on our change of control, with cooperation on successor administrative changes. Section 13 (p0056) is consistent, allowing transfer of licence rights to an Affiliate or successor under a Section 24 assignment. No walk-away features are present, so no redline is warranted.

verification.notes: No proposal: element-level redline verification is not applicable.

quote: 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
rationale: The Agreement contains no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Customer, which meets the preferred position. Clause 12.3 expressly confirms Customer may engage any supplier and has made no exclusivity, non-compete or minimum-volume commitment, and clause 2.1 confirms there is no minimum quantity or purchase commitment and that declining further Order Forms is not a breach. Section 4 routes Affiliate demand through Order Forms only, with no requirement that Affiliate requirements be sourced from Vendor. Clause 12.2 (Vendor shall not market a competing analytics service) is exclusivity running in Customer's favour and is acceptable per the detection guidance. Remaining "exclusive" references (non-exclusive licence in 13.1, exclusive-remedy carve-outs, exclusive jurisdiction in 28.2) are unrelated to exclusive dealing. No redline needed.

verification.notes: No proposal: element-level redline verification is not applicable.

quote: 13.3 Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.
rationale: Section 13 meets the preferred position in full. The subscription grant (13.1) expressly extends to Customer, its Affiliates and contractors acting on their behalf, with no notice precondition; paid-up software and embedded Vendor Technology (13.2) is licensed perpetually, irrevocably and royalty-free to Customer and its Affiliates with contractor support permitted; and 13.3 allows transfer to an Affiliate or successor under the Section 24 assignment right and limits revocation/suspension to a material uncured payment or use breach after notice and a cure opportunity. Termination rights in Section 9 do not create any at-will revocation in Vendor's favour (9.1 requires uncured material breach; 9.4 is a Customer-side right). No redline required.

verification.notes: No proposal: element-level redline verification is not applicable.

quote: 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
rationale: The agreement contains no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on us. Clause 12.3 goes further and expressly confirms that nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, or conducting business in any field or territory, and that no exclusivity, non-compete, MFC, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment has been made. The only competition restriction (12.4) binds Vendor and benefits us, so it is not flagged. The sole Customer-side prohibition elsewhere (13.4, reverse engineering of hosted source code, subject to the statutory carve-out) is a standard IP protection, not a field-of-use or non-compete restriction. This meets the preferred position.

verification.notes: No proposal: element-level redline verification is not applicable.

quote: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form without cause by delivering the written notice specified in Section 29.4. Customer owes only accrued Fees, and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the period after termination.
rationale:
Meets the preferred position. Section 9.4 gives Customer an unconditional right to terminate the Agreement or any Order Form without cause; Section 29.4 fixes that notice period at thirty days, matching our preferred 30-day standard. Customer owes only accrued Fees (no early-termination fee or penalty), and Vendor must refund prepaid Fees for the post-termination period, reinforced by Section 10.2 (refund of prepaid recurring Fees). This is important given the three-year term in Section 8.1.

Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right at all: searches for "convenience", "without cause" and "Vendor may terminate" return no Vendor-side right, and Sections 9.1-9.3 limit Vendor to material breach and insolvency. Section 24.4 also bars Vendor from terminating on Customer's change of control, and Section 20.5 bars Vendor from terminating unaffected Services. So the walk-away risks (no Customer convenience right in a multi-year term; short-notice Vendor convenience right) are both absent.

Two drafting points noted rather than flagged under this rule: (1) the 30-day notice period sits in the Notices section (29.4) rather than in 9.4 itself, which is awkward but substantively correct; (2) the Section 1.5 definition of "Fees" as only the USD 12,000 Implementation Fee is inconsistent with its use throughout (7.1, 8.3, 10.2 all refer to recurring/Order Form Fees) and, read literally, would narrow the 9.4 refund. That defective definition is a document-wide issue better addressed under the definitions/fees rules than as a termination-for-convenience deviation, since this rule's material terms (who may terminate, notice period, early-termination fee) all sit at or above preferred. Section 7.7's late-payment liquidated damages is a payment-terms matter, not a convenience-termination penalty, and is not double-flagged here.

verification.notes: No proposal: element-level redline verification is not applicable.

quote: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.
rationale: § 22 is the only audit right binding us and it meets the preferred position on every material term: frequency capped at once per twelve months, thirty days' prior written notice, normal business hours, off-site where practicable via an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds five percent, and no direct access to Customer systems, unrelated Customer Data, privileged material or third-party confidential information (p0095). § 22.3 additionally treats findings as our Confidential Information and limits their use. § 23 (Records and Customer Assurance) contains no counterparty audit right, and no other inspection, verification or remote-monitoring language binding us exists in the document. No redline needed.

quote: The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction, and each Party irrevocably submits to personal jurisdiction and waives any objection based on venue or inconvenient forum.
rationale: Section 28.1 selects the laws of the State of New York and 28.2 grants exclusive jurisdiction to the state and federal courts in New York County — exactly our preferred position on both law and forum. No arbitration provision appears anywhere in the document (a search for "arbitration" returns no results), so there is no foreign-seat arbitration risk. The pre-filing executive escalation step in 28.3 and the carve-out permitting interim injunctive relief in another court do not displace New York courts and expressly do not delay urgent relief or limitations-period filings; noted for information only. No redline required.

quote: 7.6 Vendor warrants that Fees charged to Customer will be no less favourable than fees offered to any similarly situated customer for comparable volumes and terms.
rationale: The sole most-favoured-nation provision (§ 7.6) is granted by Brightline in our favour: Vendor warrants that Fees charged to us will be no less favourable than those offered to similarly situated customers, with a reasonable comparability qualifier ("comparable volumes and terms"). Nothing in §§ 4, 7 or 30, or elsewhere in the document (searches for "favourable", MFN, match-rights and third-party-terms language returned no other hits), obliges Northwind to extend Brightline best terms given to any third party or to match third-party offers. This meets the preferred position — no MFN obligation burdens the Customer — so no redline is proposed; the Vendor-granted MFN is retained as beneficial to us.

quote: No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.
rationale: The Agreement meets the preferred position: § 2.1 expressly states that no minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies, that Customer pays only for Services ordered under a signed Order Form, and that declining to place further orders is neither a breach nor a shortfall. This is reinforced by § 7.1 (Vendor may not impose an unstated minimum-use charge) and § 12 (acknowledgement that Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment). There is no take-or-pay, shortfall penalty, no-downgrade-at-renewal, or volume cap on Customer usage: § 8.2 renewals are terminable on thirty days' notice by Customer with no quantity floor, and § 13 contains no usage caps. No redline required. (Separately noted, not under this rule: § 7.7 late-payment liquidated damages of fifteen percent of annual Fees per week is an unrelated payment-terms issue for the applicable rule.)

quote: 8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand.
rationale: Renewal mechanics sit at the preferred position: renewal terms are successive twelve-month periods (no multi-year auto-renewal), Customer alone may opt out on just thirty days' written notice, and Vendor must send a renewal reminder sixty days beforehand (with the opt-out deadline extended if the reminder is missed, which further benefits us). Renewal price increases in § 8.3 are capped at the lesser of CPI and three percent, with ninety days' notice and no increase on prepaid periods, matching the preferred uplift cap. No redline needed.

quote: 11.1 Upon expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at the rates in the expiring Order Form. Assistance includes knowledge transfer, export support, cooperation with a replacement supplier, orderly migration, and continued service at the then-current scope and service levels.
rationale: Section 11 meets the preferred position in full: six months of transition assistance on Customer's request (at the expiring Order Form rates, which is better for us than "then-current rates"), return of all Customer Data in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format within thirty days, and secure deletion with written officer certification. Deletion is triggered only after Customer confirms successful return, and Vendor may not withhold Customer Data over a fee dispute, so the walk-away risks (no data return, immediate deletion, assistance conditioned on payment) are absent. Section 10.1 preserves access through the agreed transition period and Section 15 imposes no conflicting deletion timing. No redline needed.

quote: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.
rationale: Section 19 meets the preferred position on every material term. Vendor warrants Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel in accordance with industry standards (19.1), and that Services and Deliverables will materially conform to documentation and specifications. The conformance period is ninety days after delivery or acceptance (whichever is later) for Deliverables and the full subscription term for Hosted Services (19.2) — at or above the preferred 90-day services / 12-month software benchmark. Section 19.3 adds no-malicious-code and compliance with Applicable Law warranties. Section 19.4 supplies a real remedy ladder: prompt re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, and termination plus refund of Fees paid if Vendor cannot cure in a reasonable period, expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims. The disclaimer in 19.5 is mutual, limited to implied warranties, and expressly does not limit any express warranty, service level, indemnity or remedy, so it does not swallow the express warranty. Acceptance testing in Section 6 independently reinforces the refund path. No redline warranted.

rationale: Section 18 contains a full vendor insurance clause that meets the preferred position on every material term: Vendor-funded coverage for the term plus one year, commercial general liability of USD 1,000,000 per occurrence / USD 2,000,000 aggregate, professional errors and omissions of USD 2,000,000, cyber and privacy liability of USD 5,000,000 (Brightline processes Customer Data), and workers' compensation as required by law. Section 18.2 adds certificates of insurance on request, which the preferred position expects. The clause also exceeds the preferred position with employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, a reputable-insurer and primary-coverage requirement, advance notice of cancellation or material reduction, and confirmation that insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities — all of which benefit us. rationale: Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages payable by us of 15% of annual Fees per week of delay, triggered by a minor breach (late payment of any invoice) and uncapped, so it can quickly exceed the remaining contract value — walk-away territory under the rule, well short of both the preferred (no Customer-payable LDs) and fallback (single early-termination amount capped at three months' fees) positions. The edit is confined to the operative payment obligation in 7.7; the trigger language and the balance of Section 7 (including ordinary late-payment interest) are untouched, so no unrelated commercial term is impaired. quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable by Customer under the first Order Form during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
rationale: The cap is mutual and the carve-outs in § 21.3 (confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) plus the payment-obligation carve-back meet the preferred position on those elements. However, the cap basis fails even the fallback: "Fees" is defined (§ 1.5/1.6) as only the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee, and the cap is further limited to amounts under "the first Order Form", so the ceiling is roughly USD 12,000 regardless of actual spend — far below 6 months' fees and effectively illusory. We made the minimal edit to § 21.1 to base the cap on all amounts paid or payable under the Agreement in the preceding twelve months with a USD 1,000,000 floor, leaving mutuality, exclusions and Excluded Claims untouched.

verification.notes: Cap edit in 21.1 is a precise, minimal re-basing: it replaces the narrow first-Order-Form/defined-"Fees" basis with the exact preferred greater-of formulation (lowercase fee basis, claim anchor, USD 1,000,000 floor). All preferred carve-outs, mutuality and the mutual indirect-damages exclusion were already present in 21.2-21.3 and were correctly left untouched. The second operation is not needed to complete the preferred level and moves against our client: the original wording ("obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services") already carved Customer payment duties out of the cap while preserving the "undisputed" and "conforming Services" qualifiers. Broadening it to all "payment obligations" strips customer-favourable limits, so minimality fails on this edit. Recommended fix: drop operation 2 and retain the original 21.3 carve-back sentence; the preferred payment-obligations element is substantively satisfied by it, and any residual gap is a rationale note rather than a redline.
